title: Geo-fluid failover: session-aware telemetry-driven traffic shift
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a telemetry-driven, graceful cross-region traffic shift for the hosted API edge gateway that preserves streaming session continuity, enforces SLO-aware circuit breakers, and applies staged load-shedding when necessary. Goal is to reduce failover-induced tail-latency and minimize session resets for websocket/HTTP-2 streams while guaranteeing error-budget-aware routing decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry signal design documented and merged: latency p95/p99, error-rate, e2e session-drop, backend-capacity-utilization

Gateway can perform non-disruptive weighted traffic shifts across two active regions with session affinity fallback within 10s for new requests and < 5% session reconnection rate for live streams during steady-state shifts
Circuit-breaker rules trigger at defined SLO thresholds and cause progressive load-shedding plus routing to healthy variants, verified by chaos tests
Automated canary and rollout playbook in Console for telemetry-driven shift is available with runbook links and alerting integrations
End-to-end integration tests and a synthetic workload show <10% additional token-cost and maintain 99.9% of requests under target latency SLO during normal failover scenarios
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff meeting with Reliability, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed scope: telemetry signals, routing policies, session affinity model, streaming handling, and runbook.

2025-02-22: Drafted signal list and thresholds. P95 latency, P99 latency, 1m error-rate, error-budget burn (30m window), queue-length on gateway, kv-cache hit rate. Posting design doc: https://confluence.redwood/example/geo-fluid-failover-design

2025-02-26: Prototype routing policy implemented in gateway simulator. Added weighted-shift API and session-affinity metadata token to request headers. Simulator tests show gradual weight shifts reduce p99 spikes vs immediate cutover.

2025-02-28: Design review feedback from Security and PM. Security asked for KMS usage where we persist session affinity tokens and audit log for shifts. PM requested alternate fallback to a regional 'stateful-relay' set for long-lived streams.

2025-03-01: Created feature branch and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/6182. Initial unit tests passing. Integration tests failing on websocket drain sequence — investigating ordering with TCP proxy.
2025-03-03: Implemented circuit-breaker backoff policy and early throttling for noisy tenants. Updated docs and added dashboard panels in Grafana: https://dashboards.redwood/g/xyz/geo-failover
comments: Marco Ruiz (Runtime): We should avoid adding per-session DB lookups on the critical path; prefer a signed affinity token carried by the client and validated at the edge.
Sofia Green (Console PM): Console needs an operator view showing current weight distribution, error budget burn, and a one-click abort to revert shifts.
Lina Chen (Assignee): Plan to add a streaming drain coordinator that signals active workers to finish open segments before moving their weights down. Will prototype with the simulator first.
Security (review): Ensure session-affinity tokens are short-lived and HMAC-signed; persist only a minimal audit trail for debug. No PII to be stored.
QA: Need synthetic test harness that simulates tens of thousands of held-open streams to validate reconnection metrics under partial region outage.
